events.content:
Ship→Peek updates are not real-time and cannot explain themselves. Source ticket: PEEK-109.

## The actual diagnosis

There is no polling. Peek reads the relay **once per topic mount** and never again — `useTopicView.tsx` keys its sync effect on `[topicId, topicFolderId, relayUrl, convex]`, none of which change while you sit in a topic. "Replies take time to appear" is really "replies appear on remount", which is why a reload fixes it.

Four independent staleness sources, each matching a reported symptom:

1. **Messages/replies** — one fetch per mount (`useTopicView.tsx:144-159`). Reactions and deletions are additionally capped to the newest 100 messages per topic (`convex/nostr/sync.ts:41`), so an older message never picks up a reaction at all.
2. **Ship projects/issues in the sidebar** — `TopicProjectPanel.tsx:250-269` resolves once, keyed on a folder id that never changes. The file admits it: "the panel reflects the moment it resolved and does not live-update". A project created in Ship after the panel mounted never appears.
3. **Everything outside topics never syncs at all** — the only relay-read call sites are `useTopicView` (channel) and `AuthGate` (profiles). DMs, inbox, Desk and Screener have no read path.
4. **Auth failure is silent** — `useTopicView.tsx:150` calls `validToken()` and returns with no signal; relay failures below are `console.warn`. Silent refresh exists (PEEK-108) but it is a `setTimeout`, which browsers throttle in background tabs. The UI cannot distinguish "nothing changed" from "I stopped being able to ask".

## What is already true (verified live, 2026-08-21)

- `wss://estiva.estiva.app` accepts a WebSocket upgrade through Cloudflare from Peek's origin and immediately sends `["AUTH","<challenge>"]`. Verified with curl; **pass `--http1.1`** or the same request returns NIP-11 JSON, because `Connection`/`Upgrade` are not HTTP/2 headers.
- NIP-11 reports `supported_nips` including 42, `auth_required: true`, `max_subscriptions: 1024`, `max_filters: 10`.
- **One subscription covers messages, reactions AND deletions.** `buzz-core/src/filter.rs:68-90` has an explicit `#h` fallback to `StoredEvent.channel_id` for events carrying no `h` tag (kind:7, kind:5, whose channel is derived at ingest). So `{"#h":[channelUuid]}` delivers messages + reactions + deletions + assertions in one REQ. The current HTTP path needs four sequential round trips to do less.
- **The projection is reusable unchanged.** PEEK-106 already split credential from projection: `importChannel` / `importReactions` / `importResolutions` take events, not tokens.
- **Convex is already reactive.** Once a row lands, every open view updates. The only missing link is relay→Convex.

## Two gates

**Gate 1 — Estiva ID must sign kind:22242 (blocking).** `estiva-id/src/db/seed.ts:79` gives Peek `[9,7,5,9007,27235,1851,9101,9002]` — no 22242, so Peek cannot answer the AUTH challenge and every REQ returns `auth-required`. The socket looks healthy and delivers nothing. Deploying needs a **manual re-seed**: `update.sh` runs `migrate`, never `seed`. Unlike PEEK-128 this is only one gate — AUTH never goes through `ingest.rs`, `Kind::Authentication` is built into `buzz-auth/src/nip42.rs:52`, so no Buzz change and no relay deploy.

**Gate 2 — one subscription per channel (silent trap).** `buzz-relay/src/handlers/req.rs:1013` returns `None` when filters name more than one distinct `#h`; `subscription.rs:84-113` then registers the subscription as *global*, and `fan_out_scoped:273-288` consults only the channel indexes for channel-scoped events. The invariant is stated at `subscription.rs:321-325`. A multi-channel subscription returns correct history at EOSE and then receives **zero** live events. One REQ per channel; 1024 per connection is no practical ceiling.

## Why the socket stays in the browser

`convex/nostr/sync.ts:18-20` proposes an external consumer holding the socket. An identity is obtainable — `estiva-id/src/domain/roles.ts` has role identities with a client-credentials grant. But Buzz gates reads **per channel**: `handlers/event.rs:181-196` filters live fan-out through `is_member_cached(community, channel, pubkey)` and fails closed on private channels. A service identity would need membership in every topic — a product decision (a bot in every conversation), not an implementation detail. `convex/crons.ts` already reached this conclusion. Convex keeps the projection; only the socket moves.

## Shape of the fix

One shared WebSocket per tab. One subscription per open channel. Live events routed into the existing Convex import actions. Convex reactivity carries it to the UI. The HTTP path stays as the backfill on subscribe (it owns the `since` cursor and paging) and as the fallback when the socket is down — so the change is additive and a WS failure degrades to today's behaviour rather than to nothing.

Ordering caveat to design for: `created_at` is in seconds and several events routinely land in the same one (SPEC §6.2). Imports are idempotent by event id and `nostrSyncedAt` only moves forward (`convex/nostr/data.ts:523`), so live and backfill can overlap safely.

## Milestones

- **M1 — Un-gated relief.** Refetch on focus/visibility plus a short interval, in both the topic sync and the project panel; TTL the profile cache. Turns "until remount" into "within 30 seconds" and probably clears most reported symptoms. Nothing blocks this.
- **M2 — Open the 22242 gate.** Add it to Peek's allowed kinds, scoped by `relay` tag, deploy, **re-seed**, verify the row.
- **M3 — The live socket.** WS client with NIP-42 AUTH and reconnect; refcounted per-channel subscription manager; live events into the Convex projection; `useTopicView` subscribing with HTTP as backfill and fallback.
- **M4 — Honest state.** One derived connection state surfaced once, and relay read failures made visible instead of swallowed.
- **M5 — Beyond topics.** Subscriptions for the inbox, Desk and DMs, which have no relay read path at all today.

## Not yet verified

- The **live** `allowed_kinds` row for peek. `seed.ts` has no 22242; the read to confirm production matches was blocked. Run `docker compose exec -T postgres psql -U estiva_id -d estiva_id -tAc "select client_id, allowed_kinds from app_credentials"` before planning on it.
- No end-to-end 22242 signing test — needs a live user token.

Issues are filed in implementation order. Each is written to be picked up cold by Claude Code.

- Bug if you start typing and message and you switch different topic, the text is kept there, which is weird.
- If you start writing in thread and then go somewhere else and then go back to the thread to finish the message, the draft is gone

root.author: f3a38fa646debd4162125e0aed87b6d2393fb1ed9702b6875dcbc0c6529d64d1
root.body: Support code snippets in rich formatting

root.author: f3a38fa646debd4162125e0aed87b6d2393fb1ed9702b6875dcbc0c6529d64d1
root.body: Wondering how we can in meaningful non-distracting way surface is somebody react to your message with emoji. Right now, you learn about it just by accident. 😊

replies.author: a8a7d739dda599143ec2e88a1c3b2d69808cd2a50001179c786f51d00dc3c697
replies.body: I like the effect Slack has on top of the activity menu item where the emoji animates a little and disappears. You don't know on which conversation it happened but you get a signal something happened. We don't have global activity so I'm thinking maybe to have it as an entry to topic-specific activity (and DM speficic activity)?

replies.author: a8a7d739dda599143ec2e88a1c3b2d69808cd2a50001179c786f51d00dc3c697
replies.body: But activity doesn't make sense because that kind of activity is for everyone, not just you..

replies.author: f3a38fa646debd4162125e0aed87b6d2393fb1ed9702b6875dcbc0c6529d64d1
replies.body: It's not urgent. Let's sleep on this.

replies.author: f3a38fa646debd4162125e0aed87b6d2393fb1ed9702b6875dcbc0c6529d64d1
replies.body:
Few ideas
- The animation could happen on the topic itself in the sidebar. Let's say you gave me emoji in conversation in Feedback on Peek. The Feedback on Peek topic in sidebar would get this animation.
- Have dedicated section in Desk that would only be available if you have unread emoji reaction. It could be called "Reactions" and it would be just icon and if hove over, it would show a simple box where you would see the message with the reaction.

replies.author: a8a7d739dda599143ec2e88a1c3b2d69808cd2a50001179c786f51d00dc3c697
replies.body: This is so cool, I read our conversations and sending this now from Ship. Was thinking about testing it only and forgot how it looks in real conversation and how useful that is

replies.author: f3a38fa646debd4162125e0aed87b6d2393fb1ed9702b6875dcbc0c6529d64d1
replies.body: Yeah, it's so good and I think it's only the beginning. I definitely want to level-up conversation across all apps (well, now it's just ship and peek. E.g. add emoji reaction to ship or have draft messages shared across apps.

replies.author: a8a7d739dda599143ec2e88a1c3b2d69808cd2a50001179c786f51d00dc3c697
replies.body: It's good idea to turn it into React before adding extra functionality, I'll ask Claude tomorrow how much work that would be

replies.author: f3a38fa646debd4162125e0aed87b6d2393fb1ed9702b6875dcbc0c6529d64d1
replies.body: Yeah, I was planning to do the same once I'm done with the Claude integration. I think it would be wise to have basic structure same for all those apps as it will be easier to maintain and keep updating.

replies.author: f3a38fa646debd4162125e0aed87b6d2393fb1ed9702b6875dcbc0c6529d64d1
replies.body: Let's maybe chat 5 min tomorrow who will focus on what so we don't end up tackling the same stuff.

root.author: f3a38fa646debd4162125e0aed87b6d2393fb1ed9702b6875dcbc0c6529d64d1
root.body: We need to Refactor whole Ship. It was done very basically. It's not even React app. And I think it starts to bite us, so before we start implementing more features, I will try to refactor it to React codebase.
